title: 2nd Point: True Beauty in Everything and Wisdom Behind the Veil

questions.question: What is the big idea of this part?
questions.answer: Things that may look ugly can still have real beauty and wisdom.

questions.question: What are the two kinds of beauty taught here?
questions.answer: Beauty in itself and beauty seen in the results.

questions.question: If something looks unpleasant at first, what may still be hiding under it?
questions.answer: Order, wisdom, and beauty.

questions.question: In spring, what beautiful things are hidden under rain and muddy ground?
questions.answer: Many flowers and neat-growing plants.

questions.question: In autumn, what happens to small animals that lived among flowers?
questions.answer: They are taken away from their life duties.

questions.question: Why are those small animals taken away before winter?
questions.answer: So they are protected from winter’s hardships.

questions.question: What season is being prepared after autumn and winter?
questions.answer: A new spring.

questions.question: Which hard events are named as examples that can hide good things?
questions.answer: Storms, earthquakes, and plague.

questions.question: What grows because of events that seem ugly?
questions.answer: Hidden abilities and possibilities grow and come out.

questions.question: Why do people often call such events ugly?
questions.answer: They look only at the outside and think mostly about themselves.

questions.question: If one purpose of an event is for people, how many more purposes may be for Allah’s names?
questions.answer: Many more, even thousands.

questions.question: What kind of plants do people sometimes think are useless and harmful?
questions.answer: Thorny plants and trees.

questions.question: What are those thorny plants and trees really called in meaning?
questions.answer: Strong and well-prepared helpers among plants.

questions.question: What bird chasing another bird is given as an example?
questions.answer: Hawks chasing sparrows.

questions.question: What good result comes to the sparrow from that?
questions.answer: Its abilities develop.

questions.question: What do people often think about snow?
questions.answer: They think it is cold and not inviting.

questions.question: What is really hidden under snow, according to the passage?
questions.answer: Warm aims and sweet results.

questions.question: Why do some people wrongly think certain things are bad manners?
questions.answer: Because they judge only by the side that faces them.

questions.question: What should be used to understand these matters rightly?
questions.answer: Wisdom.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about things that seem mixed up or messy?
questions.answer: They may actually be arranged in a careful and meaningful way.

questions.question: What does this passage explain about everything Allah created?
questions.answer: Everything has been made in a very good way.

questions.question: Does the passage say only pretty-looking things have beauty?
questions.answer: No. Even things that seem ugly can have beauty.

questions.question: What is essential beauty?
questions.answer: Beauty that belongs to a thing itself.

questions.question: What is relative beauty?
questions.answer: Beauty that is seen in what comes from it.

questions.question: When spring comes, what is hidden under wet weather and dirty ground?
questions.answer: Lovely flowers and orderly plants.

questions.question: Why is autumn’s ending of many living things not only sad in this passage?
questions.answer: Because it also protects some creatures and prepares for spring.

questions.question: What does winter do that makes this protection meaningful?
questions.answer: It brings hard and painful conditions.

questions.question: What hidden things can come out during disasters and troubles?
questions.answer: Unseen good qualities and growing abilities.

questions.question: What mistake does a self-focused person make?
questions.answer: He judges only by what affects him.

questions.question: Why is that way of judging too small?
questions.answer: Because an event may have many other wise purposes.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the purposes of events beyond human benefit?
questions.answer: Most of their purposes are tied to Allah’s names.

questions.question: How do people often judge thorny plants?
questions.answer: They think they are bad and pointless.

questions.question: How does the passage correct that idea?
questions.answer: It says they have strength and an important role among plants.

questions.question: What lesson comes from the example of hawks and sparrows?
questions.answer: Something that looks harsh may help another creature improve.

questions.question: What lesson comes from the example of snow?
questions.answer: Something that feels unpleasant can hide much good.

questions.question: Why can a topic seem embarrassing from one side but proper from another side?
questions.answer: Because one side is about people’s feelings, but another side is about creation and purpose.

questions.question: What helps a person see that proper side?
questions.answer: Looking with wisdom.

questions.question: How are the words of the Qur’an described in this part?
questions.answer: They are full of good manners and proper teaching.

questions.question: What may be hidden under things and events that look ugly to us?
questions.answer: Fine art, beauty, and wisdom.

questions.question: What does the passage say about some things that seem disorderly?
questions.answer: They may really be ordered like meaningful writing.

questions.question: What does the passage say can be found in every created thing?
questions.answer: Some kind of true beauty.

questions.question: Are all events beautiful in the same way?
questions.answer: No. Some are beautiful in themselves, and some by their results.

questions.question: What can be under an outside appearance that seems confused?
questions.answer: Bright beauty and order.

questions.question: What season is used first to show beauty under a rough covering?
questions.answer: Spring.

questions.question: What rough coverings of spring are mentioned?
questions.answer: Heavy rain and muddy earth.

questions.question: What lovely results come from those rough spring coverings?
questions.answer: Many flowers and organized plants.

questions.question: What season is used next to show hidden mercy in loss?
questions.answer: Autumn.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the small animals among flowers?
questions.answer: As friendly little creatures.

questions.question: What mercy is shown to those little animals before winter?
questions.answer: They are spared from winter’s suffering.

questions.question: What do storms, earthquakes, and plague help bring out?
questions.answer: Hidden spiritual beauties and growing abilities.

questions.question: Why do people miss the good in those events?
questions.answer: They are attached to what shows on the outside.

questions.question: What other problem makes people judge badly?
questions.answer: They think too much about themselves.

questions.question: When a person looks only at his own side, how may he judge an event?
questions.answer: He may call it ugly.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the side of events that goes beyond people?
questions.answer: It points in many ways to Allah’s names.

questions.question: What example shows that a harsh-looking struggle in nature can still be useful?
questions.answer: A hawk chasing a sparrow.

questions.question: What benefit comes to the sparrow in that example?
questions.answer: Its skills and powers grow.

questions.question: What example shows that coldness can hide kindness?
questions.answer: Snow.

questions.question: What is hidden under snow’s cold outside?
questions.answer: Good purposes and sweet results.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention embarrassment about body parts?
questions.answer: To show that people may judge by appearances and feelings only.

questions.question: What final lesson does the passage teach about things that seem messy?
questions.answer: They may really be carefully arranged and full of meaning.

questions.question: According to this passage, what should we remember when something looks ugly?
questions.answer: It may still contain beauty and wisdom.

questions.question: What are the names of the two kinds of beauty in this part?
questions.answer: Essential beauty and relative beauty.

questions.question: Which kind of beauty is about what comes later from a thing?
questions.answer: Relative beauty.

questions.question: What hidden treasures are under rainy skies and muddy land in spring?
questions.answer: Beautiful flowers and well-arranged plants.

questions.question: What does the passage say is hidden behind autumn’s hard changes?
questions.answer: Mercy for little creatures and preparation for spring.

questions.question: Why is being released from life duties a kindness for small animals?
questions.answer: It keeps them from winter’s pain.

questions.question: What does the passage say is made ready under that hard seasonal change?
questions.answer: The way for a fresh spring.

questions.question: Which upsetting events are listed to teach this lesson?
questions.answer: Storms, earthquakes, and plague.

questions.question: What can happen to hidden talents during such events?
questions.answer: They can begin to grow and bloom.

questions.question: What does the passage compare widespread change to?
questions.answer: Rain that helps unseen growth.

questions.question: Why does a person often give a wrong judgment about such events?
questions.answer: Because he loves outward looks and is centered on himself.

questions.question: If an event does not seem good for a person, does that mean it has no good purpose?
questions.answer: No. It can have many other purposes.

questions.question: What is the example of something people see as harmful in plant life?
questions.answer: Thorny plants and trees.

questions.question: What is wrong with calling those plants meaningless?
questions.answer: They actually have strength and an important job.

questions.question: What animal example shows growth through difficulty?
questions.answer: Sparrows being chased by hawks.

questions.question: What does that chase help the sparrow do?
questions.answer: It helps it develop its abilities.

questions.question: Why is snow a good example in this passage?
questions.answer: It looks unpleasant but hides great benefits.

questions.question: What problem comes from judging everything only by how it seems to us?
questions.answer: We may call good and proper things ugly or rude.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the Qur’an’s expressions?
questions.answer: They fit true wisdom, good manners, and proper conduct.

questions.question: How does the passage describe apparent disorder in the end?
questions.answer: As something that may truly be orderly and meaningful.

questions.question: What truth about creation is taught in this section?
questions.answer: All creation has beauty in some way.

questions.question: Can something seem ugly on the outside and still be beautiful in another way?
questions.answer: Yes. Its results or hidden side can be beautiful.

questions.question: What does the passage say is hidden under some ugly-looking events?
questions.answer: Beauty and order.

questions.question: In the spring example, what do rain and mud lead to?
questions.answer: Flowers and healthy plants.

questions.question: In the autumn example, what is one good result of loss and separation?
questions.answer: Small animals are kept safe from winter hardship.

questions.question: What future blessing is being prepared after autumn passes?
questions.answer: The next spring.

questions.question: What hard events are named to show that trouble can carry hidden good?
questions.answer: Storms, earthquakes, and plague.

questions.question: What do these hard events help bring out in living things or people?
questions.answer: Hidden abilities and possibilities.

questions.question: Why does a person often think only the outside matters?
questions.answer: Because he loves appearances.

questions.question: Why else does he judge wrongly?
questions.answer: Because he thinks about himself first.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the number of purposes in events that relate to Allah’s names?
questions.answer: They are very many.

questions.question: What kind of plants are used to show that people may judge wrongly?
questions.answer: Thorny plants and trees.

questions.question: What better way should we think about those plants?
questions.answer: As strong and useful parts of creation.

questions.question: What does the bird example teach us?
questions.answer: A hard-looking event may help another creature become stronger.

questions.question: What does the snow example teach us?
questions.answer: Cold and unpleasant things may hide beautiful results.

questions.question: Why does the passage talk about shame and proper speech?
questions.answer: To teach that not every topic is wrong in every way.

questions.question: What makes a topic proper when seen rightly?
questions.answer: Looking at its purpose in creation and wisdom.

questions.question: What book is described as the source of good manners in this part?
questions.answer: The Qur’an.

questions.question: What may be hidden beneath the outside of things and events?
questions.answer: Fine art and beautiful meanings.

questions.question: What does the last sentence say some messy-looking things really are?
questions.answer: Ordered and sacred writing.

questions.question: What does this passage want us to learn about things we dislike seeing?
questions.answer: They may have hidden beauty and wisdom.

questions.question: What are the two ways beauty is described here?
questions.answer: By the thing itself, or by the good results that come from it.

questions.question: What can be found under a covering that looks ugly or mixed up?
questions.answer: Real beauty and careful order.

questions.question: What springtime coverings hide lovely growth?
questions.answer: Rainstorms and muddy soil.

questions.question: What grows under those coverings?
questions.answer: Many flowers and orderly plants.

questions.question: What sad autumn events are said to have a hidden kindness?
questions.answer: Destruction and separation.

questions.question: Who is protected through that hidden kindness?
questions.answer: Small animals connected with the flowers.

questions.question: Protected from what?
questions.answer: Winter’s hard blows and suffering.

questions.question: What new season is made ready after this?
questions.answer: Spring.

questions.question: What difficult events are said to open hidden flowers that are not physical?
questions.answer: Storms, earthquakes, and plague.

questions.question: What else grows through those hard events?
questions.answer: Seeds of hidden potential.

questions.question: Why do people often miss this hidden good?
questions.answer: They pay attention only to outward appearance.

questions.question: How does being self-centered affect judgment?
questions.answer: It makes a person judge by his own benefit only.

questions.question: Does the passage say human benefit is the only purpose of events?
questions.answer: No. There are many more purposes beyond that.

questions.question: Which plants are wrongly thought to be only harmful?
questions.answer: Thorny plants and trees.

questions.question: What noble role is given to those plants?
questions.answer: They are like strong defenders among plants.

questions.question: What does the example of hawks and sparrows show about challenge?
questions.answer: Challenge can help abilities grow.

questions.question: What does the example of snow show about unpleasant things?
questions.answer: They can hide warm good and sweet results.

questions.question: Why can some things seem improper to people but still be right in another sense?
questions.answer: Because people look at shame from their side, not from the side of creation and purpose.

questions.question: How should we look at creatures and events that seem ugly?
questions.answer: With wisdom, so we can see the beauty, art, and order in them.
